articles.title: Angel Reese breaks two WNBA rebounding records in one night during Dream win
articles.summary: 24-year-old breaks single game and single season record. Reese’s 26 rebounds help Atlanta to win over Los Angeles. Angel Reese rebounded her way into the record books not once, but twice in one night.
body: “Last time I was here, I didn’t miss any shots. Tonight I couldn’t hit [anything] so I knew I was going be able to get them on the rebounding side,” Reese said after the game. “I just want to be there for my team. Offensively, defensively, whatever it takes to win.”
Reese surpassed Chamique Holdsclaw’s record of 24 rebounds, set in May 2003 for Washington. Reese now has 458 rebounds on the season, seven more than A’ja Wilson’s mark set in 2024.
“That’s a talent,” Dream guard Allisha Gray said. “I’m just in awe watching her rebound.”

A three-time WNBA All-Star, Reese set a WNBA rookie record with 13.1 rebounds per game and the all-time league record with 15 straight double-doubles with Chicago in 2024. She led the league in rebounding her first two seasons and is leading again this season at 12.4 per game.

articles.title: Study finds that one in four former NFL players suffers from degenerative brain disease CTE
articles.summary: 215 of 235 donated brains showed signs of CTE. Condition can only be diagnosed after death. Symptoms include problems with memory and mood. At least one in four former NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 was found to have had chronic ⁠traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), according to a study…
body: Out of the 878 former players who died during that time frame, 235 donated their brains for study, researchers said, with 215 ⁠of those donated brains ⁠found to have CTE, ​a degenerative disease that can only definitively be diagnosed after death. CTE is associated with repeated blows to the head, including concussions. Symptoms include difficulty with attention and memory, dementia, mood disorders and headaches.
An NFL spokesperson said: “The NFL continuously strives to make the game of football safer, including by implementing ⁠strategies to reduce concussions and head impacts.
“The NFL remains committed to ensuring that the NFL community has access to a robust - and expanding - set of resources to enhance their physical and ⁠mental well being.

The study’s lead author Daniel Daneshvar, the chair ‌of physical medicine and rehabilitation ‌at Mass General Brigham and an associate professor at Harvard Medical School, said that repeated traumatic brain injuries are ‌a known factor in elevated rates of neurodegenerative disease.

articles.title: Brain disease in dead NFL players 'higher than previously shown'
articles.summary: A new study says at least one in four ex-NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 had a degenerative brain disease but the true figure could be much higher.
body: As many as 97.7% of NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 could have had brain disease related to repeated blows to the head, a new study says.
Researchers looked at 878 former players who died during that period, with 235 having donated their brains to research.
Of those, 215 were found to have chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), a degenerative brain disease which can only be diagnosed after death.
The study, published in the British Medical Journal, external, also found dementia was common among brain donors.

articles.title: Sir Billy Boston, first rugby league player to receive knighthood, dies aged 92
articles.summary: Boston was one of the finest players in the sport’s history. Scored almost 500 tries for club and country. Sir Billy Boston, the Wigan Warriors legend who last year became the first rugby league player to be awarded a knighthood, has died at the age of 92.
body: The Welsh Rugby Union confirmed the news of Boston’s death on Tuesday, writing: “Sir Billy Boston, one of the best loved and most iconic figures in the history of Welsh sport, has passed away peacefully at the age of 92.

“The most famous son of Tiger Bay, he died overnight in hospital in his adopted home for the past 74 years, Wigan. His death came only four days after the funeral of his wife, Lady Joan, to whom he had been married for 70 years.”

Boston was one of the finest players in the sport’s history, scoring 478 tries in 488 appearances for Wigan during a glittering career in the 1950s and 1960s that saw him become one of the great stars of the game. Only one man, Brian Bevan, has more tries in rugby league’s history than Boston and his tally for Wigan is unlikely to ever be beaten.

Those achievements in the game saw him recognised first with an MBE in 1996, before he was awarded a knighthood for services to rugby league last summer. At the time of the award the then prime minister, Keir Starmer, described it as a “historic wrong” that the sport had waited so long for a knighthood.

articles.title: FA approves WSL academy sides in National League
articles.summary: Women's Super League (WSL) academy sides will play in tier three of the football pyramid from the 2027-28 season with the divisive proposal approved by the Football Association.
body: Women's Super League (WSL) academy sides will play in tier three from the 2027-28 season after the divisive proposal was approved by the Football Association.

Four professional game academy (PGA) sides will be given the opportunity to compete without eligibility for promotion as part of reforms to the Women's National League (WNL) which are "designed to strengthen the women's football pyramid, raise standards across the league, and improve the development pathway for young players".

Fifty two of the 72 WNL clubs signed a letter to the FA opposing the proposal to introduce top-tier academy teams in their system in June 2026, describing it as "morally wrong" and claiming "board representatives did not consult their clubs".

However, the FA has gone ahead with the plan following an "extensive consultation process with clubs and stakeholders", with the reform addressing the lack of competitive minutes young English players receive compared with their counterparts across Europe.

articles.title: Vondrousova appeals to Cas against four-year ban
articles.summary: Former Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova did not let an anti-doping official enter her home to carry out a test in December 2025 and her ban is set to run until June 2030.
body: Former Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova has appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) against her four-year ban for refusing an anti-doping test.

The 27-year-old was handed the ban in June after the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) charged her with denying a doping control officer entry to her home to conduct an out-of-competition test in December 2025.
Cas confirmed to BBC Sport that it had received the appeal but said a hearing date had not yet been set.

Vondrousova, who in 2023 became the first unseeded player to win the Wimbledon women's singles title, said in April that when she refused the test she was at "breaking point after months of physical and mental stress".

articles.title: Conflicting reports emerge over Zetterer’s potential Leeds move
articles.summary: Just one year after joining Eintracht Frankfurt from Werder Bremen, Michael Zetterer could be on the move again. According to Kicker, the 31-year-old goalkeeper is expected to make the switch to Leeds United before the transfer window closes, with a €5 million transfer fee being discussed.
body: Interestingly, Zetterer’s agent, Nico Pellatz, played down speculation over a move to Leeds for his client in an interview with Bild on Friday.

“We are very surprised by reports that Michael Zetterer is supposedly close to a move. They are not true. Michael and his family feel very comfortable in Frankfurt. A move is currently not an option for him,” he said.

Sky Germany also paints a different picture. The broadcaster reports that Zetterer’s salary could be a stumbling block to the deal, while adding that the goalkeeper himself is not pushing for a move and would prefer to remain in Frankfurt and compete for the No. 1 spot unless the situation changes significantly.
Kicker, meanwhile, believes it would be surprising to see Zetterer remain at Eintracht Frankfurt beyond the end of the transfer window given recent developments.

articles.title: Xabi Alonso brings real promise but one glaring problem could jeopardise his Chelsea rebuild
articles.summary: Alonso could be nurturing one of the most dangerous attacks in the league but has a long-standing problem to solve at the other end of the pitch
body: Xabi Alonso came to Craven Cottage hoping for another Premier League first. Twenty-two years earlier, he bagged his first English top-flight goal for Liverpool. Against a former Reds teammate striving for the same goal, Alvaro Arbeloa, he created another happy memory on his managerial bow.

Most pictured his return to England to come with Liverpool; Chelsea fans already seem grateful he’s landed in London. While far from the perfect performance, victory in a five-goal thriller against Fulham brought a lot of encouragement.

A mixture of big spending and summer snubs seems to have forged one of the most dangerous attacking front threes in the league. Morgan Rogers showed signs he was worthy of his £117m price tag. Cole Palmer, with a point to prove after his World Cup omission, suddenly looked like a real problem again after what was, by his standards, a dud of a season. His link-up with Joao Pedro took effect within 31 seconds.

articles.title: Baumgardner to face undefeated Turhan as blockbuster Dubois showdown nears
articles.summary: Alycia Baumgardner will move up a division to fight Elif Nur Turhan for her IBF lightweight world title on November 8 in a seismic move that brings a blockbuster showdown with Caroline Dubois a step closer.
body: Baumgardner, the reigning unified WBO, WBA and IBF super featherweight world champion, will jump up five pounds to the 135lbs division to face the undefeated Turhan in the headline bout of MVPW-07 at College Park Center in Arlington, Texas.
"When I set my mind to something, I see it through, and 135 will be no different," Baumgardner said. "This is a super fight, the kind of fight boxing deserves, and the beginning of my next chapter.
"I know what it takes to become undisputed. I've done it before, and I'll do it again."

Turhan added: "Alycia is a boxer who steps into the ring determined to win, never even entertaining the possibility of defeat. I know I am facing an opponent who steps into the ring solely for victory.

articles.title: MLB playoff format is flawed & needs to be fixed immediately
articles.summary: The MLB playoff format has done some good things for the sport. Expanding the postseason to six teams per league creates more meaningful games, and rewarding division winners with playoff berths is absolutely the right idea. The problem isn’t who gets into the playoffs.
body: The 2026 American League race has exposed that flaw in a major way.
There is nothing wrong with guaranteeing playoff spots to division winners. If a team wins its division over 162 games, it deserves to be rewarded with a postseason berth.
The problem is that winning a weak division can be more valuable than having one of the best records in the league.
Under MLB’s current format, the top two division winners receive byes into the Division Series, while the third division winner and three Wild Card teams play in the best-of-three Wild Card round.
points: The MLB playoff format has done some good things for the sport.
Expanding the postseason to six teams per league creates more meaningful games, and rewarding division winners with playoff berths is absolutely the right idea.
The 2026 American League race has exposed that flaw in a major way.

articles.title: Littler and Van Gerwen to headline World Series of Darts Finals
articles.summary: Luke Littler, Michael van Gerwen and Gerwyn Price will headline a packed field competing for a top prize of £100,000 at the 2026 World Series of Darts Finals.
body: The event, which has a £450,000 prize pot, will return to the AFAS Live in Amsterdam and is set to take place between September 17-20.
Reigning champion Van Gerwen will be out to defend his title on home soil after he bested Littler in last year's final to scoop an £80,000 cheque at last year's event.
Van Gerwen has been in excellent form on the circuit this year, having already won the Bahrain Darts Masters in January and the Nordic Darts Masters in June.
He also came close to winning the inaugural Saudi Arabia Darts Masters in January, but was bested by Littler 8-5 in the final.

articles.title: 'Not the best version of me' - Hamilton regrets frustrated Dutch GP comments
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton says he didn't present "the best version" of himself when criticising his Ferrari team over the radio and in television interviews at the Dutch Grand Prix.
body: Hamilton sounded irate in a series of radio messages sent when he was being held up by team-mate Charles Leclerc despite the pair being on different strategies during the race in Zandvoort.

The seven-time world champion felt as though the lost time ultimately cost him a podium as he finished fourth just behind George Russell having been unable to overtake the Mercedes in an exciting finale.

Hamilton, who joined Ferrari from Mercedes in 2025, doubled down on his criticism of his team after the race when he compared the Italian squad's hesitation to get Leclerc out of his way to the Silver Arrows decisively ordering Russell to let his team-mate, championship leader Kimi Antonelli, pass him later in the race.

Reflecting on the weekend an in Instagram post on Monday, Hamilton said: "I've listened back to some of my radio and TV comments. In the heat of the moment frustration can come out, especially when you care as deeply as I do.
